quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, drivers must follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light. This is one of the few times drivers do not follow traffic signals.

questions.question: What color are highway signs that show how far away the next exit is?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Highway signs that show where you are going are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Follow the car ahead more closely.
Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, do not make sudden changes in speed or direction. Slow down and do not use cruise control. These actions help you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, when should you proceed?

options.text: When you can see all the tracks clearly.
After you stop on the first track and check for another train.
As soon as the first train passes.
When one of the tracks is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see all the tracks clearly.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, wait until you can see all tracks clearly before crossing. Do not proceed just because one train has passed. Another train may be coming on a different track.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycles is true?

options.text: It is okay for other drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle is more balanced with two riders than with one.
When passing a motorcycle, you must move completely into the other lane.
Motorcyclists do not always use their brake lights when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: When passing a motorcycle, you must move completely into the other lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane of space. When you pass a motorcycle on the left, your entire vehicle must be in the left lane before you start passing.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during the day.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going in the same direction. You can cross these lines to change lanes or pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How can you help prevent another car from hitting you from behind?

options.text: Avoid stopping suddenly.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before you stop.
Let your car slow down before you press the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: All of these actions help prevent rear-end collisions. Avoid sudden stops, check for traffic behind you, and slow down gradually to give drivers behind you time to react.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You can only drive straight.
You can only drive in the direction of the arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to move in any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can drive only in the direction shown by the arrow, but only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, let other traffic go first, and drive at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Other drivers must let you in.
Drive slowly while checking traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other traffic go first, and drive at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, signal and match the speed of traffic already on the freeway. Let other vehicles go first and merge smoothly into traffic.

questions.question: What should you do at dusk or on cloudy days?

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Use your parking lights.
Do not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk and on cloudy days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or 500 feet behind another vehicle. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?

options.text: Braking too often.
Braking suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot push water off the road. They lose grip and your car slides on a layer of water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving at night
When driving on slippery roads
When driving at high speeds
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Use a three-second following distance in good conditions. Add one second for each bad condition like night driving, wet roads, or high speeds.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Slow down to reduce the risk.

questions.question: You cannot safely pass on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle is fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street, you need clear visibility ahead, enough space to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and a vehicle that can pass safely. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, you should look toward ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road if an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your path until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because few vehicles are coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or in curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never drive on the shoulder to pass. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area
The highest or lowest speed you are allowed to drive
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in poor conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed you are allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on a road. The maximum limits are for ideal conditions. Slow down when conditions change.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement mean?

options.text: Drivers may make the movement shown by the arrow if they want to.
Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers must always stop completely before making the movement shown by the arrow.
Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the pavement shows the direction you must go from that lane. Follow all traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: When there is an oncoming car to the left and a bicyclist to the right, you should:

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Go between both.
Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and traffic.
Slow down without stopping.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. Stop completely and look for pedestrians and other traffic. Wait until the intersection is clear before going.

questions.question: Roads become very slippery:

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain has stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the road surface. Hot weather makes this worse because heat causes more oil to rise.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children:

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Accelerate quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus, watch for children walking along the side of the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction. Solid white lines cannot be crossed. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, you may pass:

options.text: Only in an emergency.
If you are on an expressway.
If traffic is clear.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: If traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you can cross it to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If a train is close or fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find an alternative route across tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you can check your blind spots by:

options.text: Using the inside rearview mirror.
Using the outside rearview mirror.
Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to check your blind spots before every lane change.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment depends on:

options.text: Whether you drink beer instead of wine.
Whether you drink wine instead of beer.
Whether you drink hard ciders or mixed drinks.
The amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: The amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol harm your reflexes and judgment. The type of alcohol does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are prohibited.
You may proceed if the way is clear.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you drive past this sign, you are going the wrong way. You could have a head-on collision. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: A person who drives much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be dangerous. On two-lane roads, if traffic is backing up behind you, pull over and let cars pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when conditions require it.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Maintain your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop off the pavement, reduce your speed without braking. Then carefully steer back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic before re-entering the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What colors do warning signs use to show upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs use yellow backgrounds with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs use orange backgrounds with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so other drivers know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers have time to see and react to your plans.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if it goes against the flagger's signals.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if there were no construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the flagger's directions.
questions.explanation: You must obey flaggers, signs, and police officers in construction zones. Failing to do so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: What should a worried, nervous, angry, or crying driver do?

options.text: Drive normally—emotions do not affect driving.
Drive faster because emotions make you more alert.
Calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
Call a friend while driving to feel better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions distract your mind from driving. Take time to calm down and get focused before you start driving.

questions.question: What should drivers do when approaching a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic crossing.
Keep driving—you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at a red light. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if there is no sign prohibiting it.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no traffic from either direction can cross it to pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What does it mean when a solid white edge line angles toward the center of the road?

options.text: An intersection is just ahead.
A construction area is coming up.
You will need to turn left soon.
The road is getting narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is getting narrower.
questions.explanation: When the edge line angles toward the center, it means the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what happens?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Both drivers should use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only alcohol levels above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only alcohol levels above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. No one can drink and drive safely.
